wWhatBody:
Self-reflection is a calm look inward: what you feel, what you think about, what matters to you. It isn't self-criticism, but attention and curiosity towards yourself.

For example, you feel irritated and ask yourself: what exactly touched a nerve? What was missing? What might help?

Writing makes thoughts clearer, and over time you can see what fills you up and what drains you.
wLead: A quiet place for your thoughts, without rush or judgement. Come back whenever you like.
w1: Page. A moment to pause and listen to yourself. You can answer questions or write freely about anything.
w2: Path. All your entries are kept here with date and time. You can reread, add to or edit them.
w3: Share. Send a copy of entries from chosen days, for example to a therapist or someone close.
w4: Appearance. Colours, dark or light mode, atmosphere, font and language, so it feels like yours.
wPrivacy: Your entries are private and encrypted on your device: without your password no one can read them, not even the app's author. Sign in with Google or email so they're saved.

legalSections: Who is responsible
Quiet Page is a non-commercial personal project by Artem Soroka (Switzerland).
Without an account
Entries, the draft and settings stay only in this browser and are not sent anywhere.
With an account

Your e-mail address (with Google sign-in, also your Google profile name and photo) and your entries are stored. Entries are encrypted on your device before they are sent, so neither the app’s author nor Google can read them.
What is not here
No ads, analytics, trackers or third-party cookies. Nobody analyses the content of your entries or passes it on.
Who processes the data

Encrypted entries are stored in Google Cloud Firestore, in Google’s data centre in Zurich (Switzerland). Sign-in is provided by Google Firebase Authentication; Google may process this data (such as the e-mail address) outside Switzerland too, including in the EU and the USA. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages; like any host, it sees technical request data such as the IP address and may also process it abroad. All of this is governed by these companies’ data protection terms.
How long it is kept
Until you delete the entries or the account. A deleted entry disappears from the database at once; it may remain for a short time in Google’s internal backups, still encrypted.
Your rights

You can view your data at any time, save it to a file (Settings → Data), change it or delete it: Settings → Account → “Delete account and all entries”. You can also contact the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).
Not therapy
This is a tool for self-reflection, not therapy, diagnosis or medical care. If things are very hard, every screen has the link “If things are very hard right now”.
Age
The app is meant for people aged 16 and over.
Beta version
The app is free and changes gradually. It is provided “as is”, without a guarantee of uninterrupted service, so it is worth saving a backup from time to time.
